record.final_answer:
Short answer: not with the SDK as we're using it. 5 seconds sits below the polling floor, so the only route is push updates, and that has a plan requirement.

What the constraint is (from the Nimbrel server SDK 4.x docs, read 2026-04-20 — the doc host doesn't resolve from this machine, so I couldn't re-verify today):

  • Default propagation is polling, every 30 seconds. A flipped toggle lands anywhere from 0 to 30s later, ~15s on average.
  • The polling interval cannot be set below 10 seconds. So no amount of tuning gets polling to 5s — this is a hard floor, not a default.
  • Push updates require stream: true in the client options, and streaming is only available on the Team plan or above.

So: 5s is achievable, but only by moving from polling to streaming, and only if we're on Team or higher. Without streaming, the realistic promise to Product is "within 30 seconds", or "within 10" if we tune the interval.

What it would take:

  1. Inventory the services. Every running service needs to be on an SDK version that supports streams; a mixed fleet means mixed propagation, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes a toggle look flaky.
  2. Plan check. Streaming is gated on Team+. If we're below that, the 5s target is a pricing decision, not an engineering one — worth surfacing to Product now rather than after the work.
  3. Enable stream: true per service, and keep polling as the fallback path for reconnect gaps. A dropped stream with no fallback silently freezes flags at their last value, which is worse than 30s polling.
  4. Audit in-process caching. This is the part that bites: if a service reads a flag once at startup or caches it in a local map, streaming delivers the update to a cache nobody re-reads and the toggle still won't take effect. Those caches need invalidation on the stream event (or a short TTL).
  5. Connection operations — reconnect/backoff, and how many concurrent stream connections the plan allows. I don't have that number; it needs checking against the plan's limits before rollout.

Caveats on the above: /stand/ws is an empty repo (single empty "initial" commit), so I had no code to confirm which SDK versions our services actually run or how they cache flag values — items 1 and 4 are unknowns I'd need to look at. And the 30s/10s/Team-plan figures rest on that April reading, so if Nimbrel has shipped a major SDK since then, the floor and the gating are worth re-checking against current docs before committing to a date.
